title: A gift, a reason, a little too much

sections.title: Saying what you think
sections.content: An *ajándék* is a gift: *Ajándékot veszek.* (I am buying a gift.) To say you like something but it has a problem, use *de* (but), with a comma: *Szép, de drága.* (Nice, but expensive.) *Egy kicsit* (a little) softens it: *Egy kicsit drága.* And to say why you do not take it, use *mert*: *Nem veszem, mert túl nagy.*

sections.title: Nice, but...
rows: I won't take it because it is too big.

items.english: The coat is nice, but expensive.
The shirt is a little big.
I won't take it because it is too small.

items.spanish: A fehér ing olcsó és szép.
items.english: The white shirt is cheap and nice.

sections.content: Put a comma before *de* and *mert*. *De* contrasts (*szép, de drága*), *és* adds (*olcsó és szép*), *mert* gives a reason.
